subject: general
question:
Based on the situation in the sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment.

He always takes up __difficult tasks – those which are beyond his capabilities__.

options.text: Bite off more than you can chew

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Bite off more than you can chew"** means **to take on a task that is way too big or beyond one's capabilities**. (अपनी क्षमता से अधिक कार्य लेना)

 
 
• **Example: **He** bit off more than he could chew** when he promised to complete the project alone in a week.
 
 

Therefore, the correct idiom for the given phrase is "**Bite off more than you can chew**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Pull someone’s leg** (मजाक में किसी को धोखा देना): Jokingly deceive someone.

 
 
• **Example:** She thought he was serious, but he was just **pulling her leg.**
 
 
 
• **No pain no gain** (मेहनत के बिना सफलता नहीं मिलती): One must work hard or endure suffering to achieve something valuable.
 
 
• **Example:** You need to exercise more if you want to lose weight; remember,** no pain no gain.**
 
 
 
• **Miss the boat** (मौका चूकना): To miss an opportunity.
 
 
• **Example:** He **missed the boat** when he didn't apply for the job in time.
